title: Computing PageRank with Damping and Power Iteration
description: Combine a 3x3 link matrix A with a uniform teleportation matrix using damping factor d = 0.85, then iterate x_new = x @ P until convergence.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import `numpy as np` and define the `3 x 3` link transition matrix `A` for three web pages.
Inside `pagerank(A, d=0.85, tol=1e-8, max_iter=100)`, build `teleport = np.ones((n, n)) / n` and blend it with `A` via `P = d * A + (1 - d) * teleport`.

Start from the uniform vector `x = np.ones(n) / n` and repeatedly multiply `x_new = x @ P`. Stop when the L1 change `np.linalg.norm(x_new - x, 1)` drops below `tol`, and print the final PageRank vector.

Look at lines 12-13 and 17-19. `P` gives every state at least `(1 - d) / n` transition probability to every other state. Power iteration stops as soon as `x_new` and `x` differ by less than `1e-8` in L1 norm.

steps.question: Look at the columns of `A`: page 2 (column index 2) receives half of page 0's link weight and all of page 1's link weight. Which of the three pages ends up with the highest PageRank score?
steps.answer: Page 2 (the third entry) gets the highest PageRank score (`0.39739966`), followed closely by page 0 (`0.38778971`, which receives all of page 2's outgoing link weight).

steps.description: Line 13 constructs the Google matrix `P = 0.85 * A + (1 - d) * teleport`.
